about: Rows for the section Cross-checks of three Method notes, in the five columns site/scripts/check-cross-checks.mjs reads (Our figure, Published figure, Source and date, Gap, Reason). 'where' and 'source_refs' and 'read' are for the reviewer and are not columns of the note.

rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, page 43; [NLR (formerly NREL), Annual Technology Baseline 2025, workbook 2025_v1](https://data.openei.org/files/8759/2025_v1_Workbook_08-27-2026.xlsx), sheet Utility-Scale Battery - R&D, row 105, column 2025

rows.reason: The page takes the midpoint of Lazard's 2-hour case. The ATB's overnight cost is one modeled system in 2023 dollars with its grid connection outside it; Lazard's is a 2025 range of its own estimates with EPC inside it
rows.where: typed default, site/lib/batterystack.ts:86 (COSTS[2]); no check-values key
rows.read: Lazard read 21 October 2026 (session 448); ATB cited in the repository: site/data/sourced_ranges.json, from the workbook retrieved 19 October 2026 (session 306)

rows.published: ATB workbook, 8 hours, Moderate, overnight USD 2,137.36 per kW (2023 dollars); Lazard prints no 8-hour case
rows.source: [NLR (formerly NREL), Annual Technology Baseline 2025, workbook 2025_v1](https://data.openei.org/files/8759/2025_v1_Workbook_08-27-2026.xlsx), sheet Utility-Scale Battery - R&D, row 114, column 2025; [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), page 43 (2 and 4 hours only)
rows.reason: Two documents of the same ATB: the page reads the cost report's 2024 dollars (Cole, Karmakar and Mann, section 2.2), the workbook states 2023 dollars and a Moderate case built from component costs. The gap is the dollar year and the case, not a fault of the model
rows.where: typed default, site/lib/batterystack.ts:88 (COSTS[8]) and site/lib/battery/finance.ts:394 (ATB); no check-values key
rows.read: ATB cited in the repository: site/data/sourced_ranges.json, from the workbook retrieved 19 October 2026 (session 306); Lazard read 21 October 2026 (session 448)

rows.published: Lazard: storage O&M USD 3.0 to 8.2 per kWh a year, USD 6.00 to 16.40 per kW at 2 hours; ATB, 2 hours, Moderate: USD 32.06 per kW a year
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, page 43; [NLR (formerly NREL), Annual Technology Baseline 2025, workbook 2025_v1](https://data.openei.org/files/8759/2025_v1_Workbook_08-27-2026.xlsx), sheet Utility-Scale Battery - R&D, row 122, column 2025

rows.reason: Two conventions, as the 4-hour row above says: Lazard leaves augmentation out of O&M and lets the battery fade; the ATB's fixed O&M is 4 percent of its capital cost a year and pays for augmentation

rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, page 43; [NLR (formerly NREL), Annual Technology Baseline 2025, workbook 2025_v1](https://data.openei.org/files/8759/2025_v1_Workbook_08-27-2026.xlsx), sheet Utility-Scale Battery - R&D, row 173, column 2025

rows.our: Breakeven toll, default case (ERCOT, 4 hours): USD 106.79 per kW-year
rows.published: Lazard's levelized cost of storage, 100 MW, 4 hours, unsubsidized, as Lazard states it per kW-year: USD 145 to 319
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, page 20
rows.reason: Lazard's own per kW-year page agrees with the row above that converts its USD 115 to 254 per MWh (USD 144.90 to 320.04). The toll covers the debt 1.25 times and the fixed O&M only; Lazard's cost also earns 12 percent on equity, pays the charging energy and taxes
rows.where: no check-values key: computed by site/lib/battery/finance.ts from the assumptions; the method note's own row of session 196

rows.our: Cycles: at most one full cycle a day, on every day of the year
rows.published: Lazard: one cycle a day at 90 percent depth of discharge, 350 days a year (126,000 MWh a year for 100 MW, 4 hours)
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, pages 43 and 47
rows.gap: 0 cycles a day; up to 15 more days a year
rows.reason: The model dispatches against each day's prices and may skip a day; Lazard fixes a duty of 350 full cycles. Its 126,000 MWh a year is the divisor the per kW-year conversion above uses
rows.where: typed default, site/lib/battery/finance.ts:96 (MODEL.cycles); no check-values key

rows.our: Investment tax credit: none by default; the sensitivity's sourced mode says "the project's own credit, none published as a range"
rows.published: Lazard's storage cases: investment tax credit (storage) 30 to 40 percent
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOS v10.0, page 43
rows.gap: -30 to -40 points at the default; the sourced mode has a published range it does not use
rows.reason: No credit is the page's ruled default and stays so (Lazard's comparison figures are unsubsidized too); the words in the sourced mode do not hold for Lazard, which prints a range on the page the other storage defaults come from
rows.where: site/lib/battery/finance.ts:548 (NO_RANGE.itc); no check-values key

rows.published: ATB, utility-scale battery storage: term debt 6.5 percent, after-tax equity returns 8.5 percent, debt service coverage 2.0

rows.gap: +1.5 points (debt); +3.5 points (equity); -0.75 (coverage)
rows.reason: The page follows Lazard's storage structure (20 percent debt at 8 percent, equity at 12 percent, ruled 12 October 2026). The ATB's lower rates and higher coverage describe a contracted project that sells under a PPA, the ATB's stated electricity sales for a battery

rows.our: Gas price: Henry Hub, the 2025 mean over 8,735 hours, USD 3.54 per MMBtu (the peaker's fuel, read hour by hour)
rows.published: Lazard's gas price for every gas-fired LCOE: USD 3.45 per MMBtu
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOE v18.0, page 8 note 3 and page 37
rows.reason: Lazard holds one price for every year of a plant's life; the page reads the price of each hour, so a year's mean is the comparable figure
rows.where: the method note's CAISO cross-check row (session 298); no check-values key

rows.our: Solar in ERCOT: 2,580 MWh sold per MW over the last twelve months, a capacity factor of 29.5 percent
rows.published: Lazard's regional capacity factor for solar in ERCOT: 24 percent; utility-scale PV: 20 to 30 percent; ATB: 19.4 percent (class 10) to 31.5 percent (class 1), 2023
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), Cost of Firming Intermittency, page 30, and LCOE v18.0, page 34; [Annual Technology Baseline 2025, utility-scale PV](https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/utility-scale_pv)
rows.gap: +5.5 points against Lazard's ERCOT figure; inside both ranges
rows.reason: Ours is the ERCOT fleet's own output over its installed capacity in EIA-930 (2,580 / 8,760 hours); Lazard's ERCOT figure is its assumed plant in that region. Why the fleet runs higher was not tested here
rows.where: ms|iso=ercot&asset=solar&mw=100&mwh=0&ds=<default>&hr=10.725&vom=4.25&fom=12.5|twelve|energy

rows.our: Wind in ERCOT: 3,028 MWh sold per MW over the last twelve months, a capacity factor of 34.6 percent
rows.published: Lazard's regional capacity factor for wind in ERCOT: 34 percent; onshore wind: 30 to 55 percent; ATB, the 2023 market average turbine: 43 percent
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), page 30 and page 35; [Annual Technology Baseline 2025, land-based wind](https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/land-based_wind)
rows.gap: +0.6 points against Lazard's ERCOT figure; -8.4 against the ATB's turbine
rows.reason: The ATB's 43 percent is the 2023 market average turbine, new; the fleet's turbines are of every age. Why they differ was not tested further here
rows.where: ms|iso=ercot&asset=wind&mw=100&mwh=0&ds=<default>&hr=10.725&vom=4.25&fom=32.25|twelve|energy

rows.our: CAISO: solar sold 2,075 MWh per MW in 2025 (23.7 percent), wind 3,125 (35.7 percent)
rows.published: Lazard's regional capacity factors for CAISO: solar 27 percent, wind 33 percent
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), Cost of Firming Intermittency, page 30
rows.gap: -3.3 points (solar); +2.7 points (wind)
rows.reason: Ours is the CAISO fleet in 2025 from CAISO's own supply by fuel and EIA-930; Lazard's figures are its assumed plants in that region. Why the fleet differs was not tested here
rows.where: the method note's CAISO rows (warehouse/analysis/generator_caiso_check.py); no check-values key

rows.our: ERCOT gas peaker, 2024: 2,105 MWh per MW under the page's rule, a capacity factor of 24.0 percent (8,784 hours)
rows.published: Lazard, gas peaking: capacity factor 15 to 10 percent
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), LCOE v18.0, page 37
rows.gap: +9.0 to +14.0 points
rows.reason: The page runs the peaker in every hour the price clears its fuel and variable cost, with no start cost, minimum run or outage; a real peaker runs less. The CAISO rows above show the same against CAISO's own study
rows.where: the method note's ERCOT peaker row (session 298); no check-values key

rows.our: ERCOT gas peaker, the toll at which coverage reaches 1.25 times: USD 8.34 per kW-month
rows.published: ERCOT's net cost of new entry for a gas peaker, as Lazard quotes it: USD 9.92 per kW-month
rows.source: [Lazard, *Levelized Cost of Energy+*, June 2025](https://www.lazard.com/media/uounhon4/lazards-lcoeplus-june-2025.pdf), Cost of Firming Intermittency, page 30 note 1
rows.reason: Net CONE is a new peaker's full capital and operating cost less its expected market revenue; our toll pays the debt 1.25 times and the fixed O&M at Lazard's midpoints and leaves equity only the margin above the debt. The two are near because both price a new peaker's fixed cost per kW-month
rows.where: no check-values key: computed by site/lib/seller/finance.ts; the method note's peaker row

rows.reason: The page follows Lazard's LCOE structure, 60 percent debt at 8 percent and equity at 12 percent (page 8); the ATB's rates are after tax and for a project selling under a PPA, the gas plant quasi-merchant

rows.our: Debt coverage target: 1.25 times (the contract price and the toll are solved for it)
rows.published: ATB debt service coverage: utility PV 1.275, land-based wind 1.375, natural gas 1.45
rows.source: [Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Financial Cases and Methods](https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/financial_cases_&_methods), "Financial Assumptions by Technology"
rows.reason: A higher target raises the contract price at which a lender is paid; the contract price rises by the change in the target times the yearly debt payment, over the energy sold
rows.where: typed default, site/lib/seller/finance.ts:288 (TARGET); no check-values key

rows.source: [Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Financial Cases and Methods](https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/financial_cases_&_methods), tax credit table
rows.gap: -40 points (solar); USD -33 per MWh (wind)
rows.reason: No credit is the page's ruled default, and Lazard's comparison figures above are unsubsidized; the ATB's values are what a reader who sets the inputs would look for
rows.where: site/lib/seller/finance.ts:113 and :115 (itc, ptc); no check-values key

rows.our: Cost of capital, the default: 9.6 percent, labelled "a generator's WACC, Lazard" (0.6 x 8 + 0.4 x 12)
rows.published: Lazard's own after-tax IRR/WACC at 60 percent debt at 8 percent and 40 percent equity at 12 percent: 7.7 percent

rows.reason: 9.6 is the pre-tax weighted cost; Lazard names 7.7 percent as the WACC of that structure, after the tax saved on interest. The label quotes Lazard's structure correctly but not the figure Lazard itself calls the WACC

rows.our: The same 9.6 percent

rows.source: [Annual Technology Baseline 2025, Financial Cases and Methods](https://atb.nlr.gov/electricity/2025/financial_cases_&_methods), "Financial Assumptions by Technology"
rows.gap: +2.1 points against the debt; +1.1 against the equity
rows.reason: A datacenter's own cost of capital is not held; the gas plant that would serve a load is the nearest published figure, and it sits under the page's default
